intro: From initial framing to public feedback: six principles for clear, accessible communication that welcomes dialogue.
boucle: Public feedback informs subsequent messages: revisit and adapt this process.

actions: Start with people
Identify their questions, experiences and vocabulary. Speak with some intended audience members before finalising the content.
Set a specific objective
Define what the content should enable: understanding an idea, discussing an issue or informing a decision.
Adapt the entry point
Choose the channel, length and detail according to audience practices, then frame a concrete question.
etapes.exemple: For people and their relatives: ‘Why might several services be needed to respond to one person’s situation?’
etapes.livrable: A short brief: audience, question, objective, channel and central message.
etapes.vigilance: One audience contains diverse experiences. Information needs and trust cannot be inferred from knowledge levels alone.

actions: State one central idea
Make the main message visible at the start and organise explanations around it.
Translate concepts
Explain jargon when first used. Include examples or diagrams when they genuinely improve understanding.
Provide useful context
Present numbers with their population and period, make sources accessible and specify the next step offered to the audience.
etapes.exemple: From intersectoral networks to a public-facing question: ‘How can the right services work together for each person’s situation?’
etapes.livrable: A one-sentence message, three supporting ideas and one main source.
etapes.vigilance: An engaging headline must remain faithful to available knowledge. Simple language can preserve necessary distinctions.

actions: Ask a genuine question
Invite experiences or questions and leave room for responses.
Organise the exchange
Explain moderation rules, the limits of the response offered and follow-up arrangements.
Use the feedback
Gather recurring questions, clarify disagreements and show how exchanges shape subsequent content.
etapes.exemple: ‘What helped you move between services? What was more difficult?’
etapes.livrable: An open question, discussion ground rules and a summary of feedback.
etapes.vigilance: Provide a respectful space and avoid publicly requesting health information or details identifying a person.

actions: Locate the knowledge
Specify what was observed, what is interpretation and what remains a hypothesis or planned project.
Make uncertainty understandable
Explain the population studied, scope of findings and important limitations in accessible language.
Prepare for corrections
Date content, retain sources and make corrections visible when errors or developments require them.
etapes.exemple: Introducing the thesis: ‘This project examines how services could organise more effectively. Results are not yet available.’
etapes.livrable: A box covering what is known, what remains unknown and why.
etapes.vigilance: Communicating uncertainty involves choices of language and context; its effect on trust cannot be guaranteed in advance.

actions: Plan alternatives early
Include what will be spoken, shown and provided in text from the scripting stage.
Prepare each format
Provide reviewed captions, transcripts and useful descriptions of visual information; ensure clear reading and navigation.
Consider real uses
Invite intended users to read or try the content, considering mobile access, languages and listening contexts.
etapes.exemple: For a network diagram: name actors and explain connections aloud, then provide an accessible text description alongside the visual.
etapes.livrable: Content accompanied by relevant text and audiovisual alternatives.
etapes.vigilance: Needs vary by medium. Unreviewed automatic captions or vague alternative text may leave essential information inaccessible.

actions: Match indicators to objectives
Distinguish reach, message comprehension, participation and perceived usefulness.
Observe understanding
Ask for a brief restatement and remaining questions, instead of relying solely on views or likes.
Revise and share next steps
Identify what needs revision, change the format or explanation and record improvements.
etapes.exemple: After a short video: ‘In one sentence, what idea do you remember? What question remains for you?’
etapes.livrable: A short review connecting objectives, audience feedback and planned changes.
etapes.vigilance: Views describe distribution. Alone, they demonstrate neither understanding, trust nor behaviour change.
